sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Construct used for heterologous expression of OR51B4; specific functional assay result not stated in the ledger clip.
sites.rationale: OR51B4 is a class-A GPCR with no signal peptide; the topology landmarks place residues 1–24 as the extracellular N-terminus and TM1 begins at residue 25. The rhodopsin tag (20 aa) is fused immediately upstream of OR51B4 residue 1 (M), placing it on the extracellular face. The paper names no specific junction residue, but the N-terminus is the sole extracellular terminus of this protein, so insert_after_residue=0 is the only consistent reading. The 24-aa extracellular N-terminal span provides ample room for the ~20-aa insert, and the junction is ≥24 residues from TM1. Full-length OR51B4 cloned into pCI-vector downstream of the 20 N-terminal amino acids of human rhodopsin, creating an N-terminally tagged full-length construct for heterologous expression (PMC5342199).

sources.claim: For the recombinant expression of OR51B4, the coding sequence was amplified via PCR from human DNA and cloned into a pCI-vector downstream of the coding sequence for the 20 N-terminal amino acids of the human rhodopsin-Tag.

literature_notes: Only one ledger line (L1) is provided. It reports a full-length, membrane-anchored OR51B4 construct with a 20-aa rhodopsin N-terminal tag, qualifying as a published tag insertion. The paper names no specific residue for the junction; because OR51B4 has exactly one extracellular terminus (the N-terminus, residues 1–24), the position is topology-derived as a prepend (insert_after_residue=0). No internal loop insertions are supported by the ledger. The three other extracellular loops (ECL1: 81–95, ECL2: 162–193, ECL3: 259–270) have no ledger-grounded insertion evidence and are therefore not proposed.
